messages.subject: Loading plot
parts:
Hi All,

I would like to interpret my results obtained from the loadingplot . The respective plot was obtained from the DAPC analysis. I want to see the structure of my population according to the sampling location. My data set is a haploid and  dominant.
I would like to find out the scale of the y axis and interpret my loci contribution according to the y axis (loadings). For example, whether there is a cut off value for these loci to be claimed as significant for the genetic variation among sampling locations.  And also I would like to know whether the scale of the y axis depends on the number of loci.

Thanking you 

Buddhika

messages.author: d192ec4b1d416345
messages.subject: Re: [poppr] Loading plot
parts:
Hello Buddhika,

DAPC is explicitly part of the {adegenet} package, but I'm happy to help out here. The loadingplot is covered in section 3.4 of the adegenet DAPC manual: https://github.com/thibautjombart/adegenet/blob/master/tutorials/tutorial-dapc.pdf

Each axis on your DAPC plot represents a discriminant function that attempts to separate your groups. The y axis of the loading plot shows you what proportion the alleles/loci contributed to one particular DA axis, and they all sum to one. There is no particular cutoff value to declare anything as having significant contribution.

I hope that helps,
Zhian
